## Kyoto 5-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A balanced Kyoto plan with temples, local food, and one low-walking day built in for knee-friendly pacing. Budget target stays within **$2,800 total** excluding international flights.

## Day-by-Day Itinerary and Spending
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Focus | Main Stops | Transit Tips | Est. Spend |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Day 1 — Apr 10 | Higashiyama welcome | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Gion evening stroll | Use subway + bus + short taxi for the steepest section | **$420** |
| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Arashiyama temples and river | Tenryu-ji, Bamboo Grove, Togetsukyo Bridge, Okochi Sanso garden | Train to Arashiyama; rent a taxi for the return if tired | **$470** |
| Day 3 — Apr 12 | Fushimi Inari + sake/food | Fushimi Inari Taisha, Fushimi sake district, Nishiki Market dinner | JR Nara Line to Inari; keep the shrine visit to the lower torii area if needed | **$390** |
| Day 4 — Apr 13 | Minimal-walking day | Kyoto Imperial Palace area, Kyoto Station food halls, tea house, river cruise or taxi loop | Use taxi and short rides only; avoid long temple walks today | **$520** |
| Day 5 — Apr 14 | Northern Kyoto temples | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Ninna-ji, final kaiseki or ramen dinner | Pre-book a taxi half-day or use bus only for single-stop hops | **$430** |

## Kyoto Itinerary with Temple, Food, and Rest Balance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

### Day 1: Higashiyama and Gion
Media: Alt=Day 1: Higashiyama and Gion, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and do a gentle start at **Kiyomizu-dera**.
- Afternoon: Walk downhill through **Sannenzaka** and **Ninenzaka**, then stop at **Yasaka Shrine**.
- Dinner: Try **yudofu**, tofu skin dishes, or a tempura set in Gion.
- Transit tip: Take the bus or subway to the area, then use a short taxi ride back if the slope feels steep.

### Day 2: Arashiyama
Media: Alt=Day 2: Arashiyama, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Visit **Tenryu-ji** early before crowds.
- Afternoon: See the **Bamboo Grove** and **Togetsukyo Bridge**; add **Okochi Sanso** only if energy is good.
- Dinner: Eat **yuba** and a soba or tofu meal near Arashiyama station.
- Transit tip: The JR train is simplest; this is a good day to use a taxi for the return.

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari and Nishiki Market
Media: Alt=Day 3: Fushimi Inari and Nishiki Market, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Go early to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and focus on the lower shrine area and first torii gates.
- Afternoon: Head to the **Fushimi sake district** for a tasting or museum stop.
- Dinner: Spend the evening at **Nishiki Market** for grilled seafood, tamagoyaki, pickles, and sweets.
- Transit tip: JR Nara Line is direct and easy; this route keeps walking compact if you limit the hill climb.

### Day 4: Low-Walking Recovery Day
Media: Alt=Day 4: Low-Walking Recovery Day, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Use a taxi to the **Kyoto Imperial Palace** area or a nearby garden with benches and flat paths.
- Afternoon: Take a slow tea break, then do a **Kamo River** or **Hozugawa-style** scenic ride if you want movement without strain.
- Dinner: Have a relaxed dinner near Kyoto Station, where food halls and elevators make logistics easy.
- Transit tip: This is the best day to rely on taxis and one short indoor stop rather than multiple temple hops.

### Day 5: Northern Kyoto Temples
- Morning: Start at **Kinkaku-ji** before it gets busy.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Ryoan-ji** and **Ninna-ji** for a quieter temple sequence.
- Dinner: End with a nicer final meal — **kaiseki**, sushi, or a rich ramen bowl.
- Transit tip: A half-day taxi is efficient here because buses can be slow and transfers add strain.

## Budget Plan for the Full Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

- Lodging, 4 nights: **$1,050–$1,250**
- Local transit and taxis: **$180–$280**
- Admission fees and temple donations: **$80–$140**
- Food and drinks: **$900–$1,050**
- Snacks, tea, and small extras: **$120–$180**
- Cushion for flexibility: **$150–$250**

Estimated total: **$2,480–$2,900**
Recommended target: **about $2,700** to stay comfortably under budget.

## Transit Tips for Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

- Use **IC card payment** on trains, buses, and many taxis for easier transfers.
- Kyoto buses can be crowded and slow; for temple-heavy days, a **train + taxi mix** is often better.
- For knee comfort, prioritize **one major site per half-day** and avoid stacking too many walking stops.
- A **taxi for the final stretch** to hilltop temples can save a lot of energy and time.
- Stay near **Kyoto Station, Gion, or Kawaramachi** for the easiest food and transit access.
